title: STEP unit prompt: a second file replaces the question of the first; the browser has no prompt; a file with no unit is read two times

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
Found in the second safety read of PR #3166 (#1874). None of these can give a wrong scale: a file with no length unit is never imported until the unit is stated.

1. **A second question replaces the first.** `crates/ui/src/state_step_units.rs:28-31` and `state.rs` (about line 4522): drop two STEP files with no unit at the same time. The second refusal writes over `step_units_ask`. The question for the first file is lost with no message on the status line, and that file is not imported. **Wanted:** a queue, or a status line that names each file that waits.
2. **The browser has no prompt.** `crates/ui/src/state_picked.rs:203`: the import from bytes (the browser file picker) calls `from_bytes` with no unit and an empty `import_file`. The user gets "import refused: ... state the unit ..." and cannot state it. **Wanted:** the same prompt for the bytes path.
3. **A fixture binding can go to the wrong file.** `state_step_units.rs:41`: while an import runs, `resolve_step_units` sets `import_as_fixture` again, and the running import of a different file can take it. The same race is on `main` in the import-as-fixture flow; the prompt adds a second way into it.
4. **A file with no unit is read two times:** one full read that ends with the refusal, then the read with the unit. A large file pays the read cost twice. **Wanted:** find the missing unit before the full read.
5. The kernel functions `read_step`, `import_step` and `import_step_model` with no unit still read a file with no unit as mm. Only kernel tests call them; the geometry layer refuses. Make them refuse too, or make them private to tests.
6. No `layout_window_step_units_prompt` test exists (the DXF units dialog and the overwrite prompt have none either).
